notes: Invariant held: every decide output (move, root visits/values, PV, groups), every applied move's events and the board after it are identical to mainline on 2,826 decision points in 3 settings. Goldens not regenerated and green.

Floating point: no change reorders any sum. Each output column still gets b[j] then x[k]*w[k][j] for k ascending with zero x[k] skipped (exactly the old loop); only which columns are processed together changed. No FMA (Rust never contracts; checked: 0 vfmadd in the .so). Pair/body loops compute the same per-element expressions in the same order; max uses `if r > m {r} else {m}` = the old `if j==0 || r > m` update.

The share of time in the net was smaller than the plan's '~40%': with the merged mainline, OPCG_PROF puts forward+fwd_tokens+fwd_body+fwd_policy at ~9.5 s of ~51 s (~19%); legal+apply ~24 s (~47%) and encode (encode+enc_onplay+enc_rel+enc_leader_legal) ~11.8 s (~23%). So -42% on the net is ~x1.1 end to end.

Tried and dropped (measured, not kept): (a) tokens cache keyed by card_idx+tok (only 9.5% of trunk computes hit; slower overall); (b) body first-layer prefix cached by scalars (33% hit but hashing cost > saved rows: fwd_body +0.18 s); (c) policy first-layer prefix cached per (si, ti) (9% hit, no gain on fwd_policy and Trunk drop got slower: removed); (d) trunk cache lookup hashing straight from the encoding without building the key (-0.07 s, within noise; reverted to keep the code smaller).

Batch evaluation of children at expansion: not done. Expansion evaluates one board at a time (the node's priors, then the leaf value from the same trunk — already shared since rs-speed-a); distinct boards never become ready together without restructuring the search. Batching would only amortise weight loads (the per-column sum order would have to stay as now).

Largest remaining levers outside this WP: (1) encode is ~23% and 82% of encodes produce an encoding already in the trunk cache (1.31M trunk hits / 1.59M encodes) — a cache keyed by a board fingerprint before encoding would remove most of it, but needs a state hash that provably covers everything encode reads; (2) CandRows (~2.9 s) is mostly search/quiesce.rs cand_owned + uuid_index/slot_index (two hash maps rebuilt per priors call) — Move-side, left to rs-speed-d; (3) callgrind shows SipHash (std RandomState) ~2.4% of instructions, mostly serde_json IndexMap of the Move JSON (rs-speed-d).

Candidate gained `pub(crate) id: Option<[u32; 16]>` (only nrel::cand_rows fills it). Candidates built elsewhere (tests) leave it None and keep the old full-bits memo key; the two key kinds have different lengths so they cannot collide. Doc comment says feats/budget must not be edited after cand_rows (nothing in the crate does).
OPCG_PROF gained n_cand and n_cand_memo_hit (only counted when OPCG_PROF=1).
Absolute latency numbers here (mainline 1x1280 160.5 s) differ from speed-merge's (139 s) because 4 pinned processes ran side by side on this container; read the ratio.
No new tests (behaviour-preserving; the equality dump is the guard, per §7.2). Equality/compare/profiling scripts were work-only (scratchpad).
Python deps (opcg_sim/requirements.txt, pytest, pytest-xdist, maturin) had to be installed in this fresh container before the gates.
